title: How to make an explainer video for your business (even if you don't sell software)
summary: Make a business explainer video without an agency: the four-part structure, script length, what to show with no product to record.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


- A business explainer answers one viewer's question in 60 to 120 seconds, in four parts: the problem, how it works, proof, and the next step.
- At around 150 words a minute, a 90-second script holds about 225 words. Time your own pace to check.
- With no product screen to record, match each line to a visual: a diagram, a chart, characters, real footage, or a presenter.
- A team's videos stay consistent when fonts, colors, voice, and caption style live in a template everyone starts from.
- An announcement video needs the news, the date, what changes for the viewer, and one action, and a press release usually holds all four.
- Clueso builds the explainer from a prompt, script, document, deck, or URL, with motion graphics, animated characters, and AI voiceover, and you edit it by chat on every plan.


You run marketing for a physiotherapy group with six clinics. The leadership team wants a 90-second homepage video that explains what happens at a first appointment, and there's nothing to screen-record. The service happens in a treatment room, with a clinician, over 45 minutes, and nobody is going to film a patient.


Most businesses are in that position. An accountancy firm, a hotel group, a parts manufacturer, and a food bank all have something to explain and no app to show. Their explainers follow the same structure a software company's would, and the difference is where the pictures come from.


The steps below work with any tool. Clueso, the agentic video platform for businesses, builds explainers like these from a brief, a script, or a document, and the last section shows how.


## What is a business explainer video?


A business explainer video is a short narrated video, usually 60 to 120 seconds, that tells a specific viewer what problem your business solves, how it works, why they should believe you, and what to do next. Each line of narration has a visual that shows what the line says, and the video makes sense with nobody from your team in the room.


If you sell software, the trade-offs are different: buyers want to see the screen they'll actually use, so a[product walkthrough video](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-walkthrough-videos) of the real product usually does more than an animated version of it. For a service or a physical process, animation is often the clearest choice, because what you're explaining is hard to film.


## How should a business explainer video be structured?


Explainers that work move through four parts in a fixed order. The viewer arrives with a problem, wants to see how you deal with it, needs a reason to believe you, and then needs to know what to do. Here's the split for the physiotherapy video.


Part


Share of 90 seconds


Example line


Problem


15 seconds


"Your back has been stiff for three weeks and you're not sure it's worth seeing anyone."


How it works


45 seconds


"At your first visit, a physiotherapist asks where it hurts, watches how you move, and explains what they found before any treatment starts."


Proof


20 seconds


"You'll see the same physio at every visit, and they'll send your doctor a summary if you want one."


Next step


10 seconds


"Book a first appointment online at any of our six clinics."


Keep the how-it-works part to three or four steps. If the process needs seven, you're looking at two videos.


Proof is the easiest part to leave out and the one a skeptical viewer is waiting for. Use a number you're allowed to publish, an accreditation, a guarantee, or a customer quote you have permission to use. In regulated industries like healthcare and financial services, get the proof lines signed off by compliance before anyone builds a scene around them.


Ask for one action at the end, because a video that closes on both a phone number and a booking link leaves the viewer choosing instead of acting. Our[animated explainer video skill](https://www.clueso.io/video-skills/animated-explainer-video) uses a five-beat version of this arc, with a hook before the problem.


## How long should an explainer video script be?


Aim for 60 to 120 seconds, and measure your own pace instead of borrowing a word count. Read one paragraph of the script aloud the way you'd say it to a customer, time it, and divide the words by the seconds, then multiply by 60.


Many narrators land near 150 words a minute. At that pace a 60-second video holds about 150 words and a 90-second video about 225, which splits roughly into 40 for the problem, 110 for how it works, 50 for proof, and 25 for the next step.


Take another 10% off so a diagram has a second or two of silence to build in. Clueso writes the script at the length you choose, and your part is checking that all four parts made it in.


## What do you show on screen when there's no product to record?


Decide the visual one line at a time. Each sentence describes something, and the table matches what it describes to a visual that suits it.


When the line is about


Show


Example


A process


A diagram that builds step by step


How an insurance claim moves from submission to payout


A number or comparison


An animated chart or infographic


Fees over 10 years under two plans


A customer's situation


Animated characters acting it out


A guest arriving late to find the front desk closed


A place or object


Your own footage, stock, or AI-generated B-roll


The factory floor, a clinic waiting room


A phrase to remember


Kinetic text


The one-line promise, the booking address


A message that needs a face


A presenter or an AI avatar


A founder's welcome


Use your own footage wherever the real thing affects the decision. A guest choosing between two hotels wants to see your actual rooms, and a stock bedroom suggests you'd rather not show them. Stock and AI-generated[B-roll](https://www.clueso.io/glossary/b-roll) suit generic context, like a delivery van on a highway.


Animated characters earn their place on subjects you shouldn't film, such as a patient's diagnosis, a customer in debt, or a workplace injury. Clueso builds[character scenes from a script or prompt](https://www.clueso.io/vs/vyond) in styles from flat 2D and soft 3D clay to silhouette and paper cut-out. For a long, dialogue-led scenario with a recurring cast you want to pose by hand, a dedicated character animation tool gives you more manual control.


Charts and diagrams do the heaviest lifting in most non-software explainers. In Clueso you describe the graphic, such as "a bar chart comparing fees under two plans," and it generates a[motion graphic](https://www.clueso.io/features/motion-graphics) you refine with follow-up prompts and time to the narration. Basic motion graphics come with every plan and Advanced with Business and Enterprise, or try one chart in the free[infographics tool](https://www.clueso.io/tools/infographics) .


An[AI avatar](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-avatars) can deliver a presenter line when nobody is free to film, but when trust in one person is the point, like the clinic's lead physiotherapist, film that person.


## How do you handle voiceover, captions, and languages?


Choose the voice before the visuals, because the narration sets the timing for everything else. A human read fits when the speaker is the point, like a founder's welcome. An[AI voiceover](https://www.clueso.io/features/ai-voiceovers) fits when the script will change or when several people make videos that should share one voice.


Either way, list the names it might mispronounce and listen for each one. Our piece on[when AI voiceover belongs in customer-facing videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/should-we-use-ai-voiceover-in-customer-facing-videos) covers the trade-off.


Caption every explainer. People play video on mute in waiting rooms and open-plan offices, and[WCAG 2.2 success criterion 1.2.2](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded.html) makes captions on prerecorded video a Level A requirement. Clueso generates[captions](https://www.clueso.io/features/video-captions) from the narration on every plan and exports SRT and VTT files.


For another language, translate the script, voiceover, captions, and on-screen text together, then have a native speaker watch each version, because a label that fits in English can overflow in another language. Clueso[translates all of those into 150+ languages](https://www.clueso.io/features/auto-translate) on every plan, including Free.


## How do you keep explainer videos on brand when several people make them?


The first explainer usually looks right because one person made it with the brand guidelines open. By the fifth video from the fifth person, the series has three narrator voices, two shades of the brand blue, and captions in whatever style the last editor liked.


Guidelines in a PDF depend on each contributor remembering to open them, so the fix is a template with the decisions made before the project opens. These are the ones worth locking:


- Colors, logo, and fonts
- One or two named narrator voices
- Caption style and position
- Intro and outro cards
- A music bed and target length for each format


Build one template per format, since an explainer and a 30-second social cut need different pacing. Review the first video from each new contributor against the template, then spot-check.

## How do you make an announcement video without hiring an agency?


An announcement video is a short explainer tied to a date. A new clinic, new opening hours, a price change, a merger, or a new service each needs four things: what's new, when it happens, what changes for the viewer, and what they should do. That fits in 30 to 60 seconds.


You probably have the script already. The announcement has been written for an email or press release, and someone has approved its wording. Cut it to those four things and keep the approved phrasing, because rewriting it restarts the approval.


Show the thing itself if it exists, like the new clinic's front door. If it doesn't, kinetic text and motion graphics carry the message, or a music-only teaser can sit above a written post that does the explaining. Clueso's[Launch Announcement Clueprint](https://www.clueso.io/clueprints/launch-announcement) is a 25-second teaser in that style.


Finish every language version before the announcement goes out. For more formats, see our[product launch video examples](https://www.clueso.io/blog/product-launch-video-examples) and, for software updates,[turning release notes into launch videos](https://www.clueso.io/blog/how-to-turn-release-notes-into-product-launch-videos) .


## How do you turn a blog post or press release into a short video?


A 900-word press release becomes about 150 words of script for a 60-second video, so most of it has to go. Keep the headline news, one supporting fact, one short quote attributed on screen, and the action. Cut the boilerplate and the background paragraphs. Make a landscape version for your site and a vertical cut of 20 to 30 seconds for social feeds.

A press release saved as a PDF or Word file works the same way through the[PDF to video converter](https://www.clueso.io/tools/pdf-to-video-converter) . Our comparison of[URL-to-video tools for business explainers](https://www.clueso.io/blog/best-url-to-video-tools-business-explainers) covers what other tools do with a link.

At Clueso, we build the explainer from whatever you already have, so nobody starts from a blank timeline. Here's how a marketing team would make the physiotherapy video.


1. **Start from what you have.** Write a prompt, paste a script, upload a[PDF, Word document, or slide deck](https://www.clueso.io/features/ppt-video) , or give Clueso a public URL, with your brand kit or a Clueprint switched on.

## Frequently asked questions


### What's the best promo video maker for a B2B company?


It depends on what the video has to show. A character animation tool suits a long, dialogue-led story, and an avatar-first tool suits a presenter reading a script. Clueso suits B2B teams making explainers, promos, and announcements from documents, decks, recordings, or prompts, with motion graphics, characters, AI voiceover, and brand templates in one place. Our roundup of[AI animated explainer video makers](https://www.clueso.io/blog/best-ai-animated-explainer-video-makers) compares named tools.


### Can I edit an AI-generated explainer video after it's made?


Yes, in Clueso. Select any part of the video and tell Clueso AI what to change, and the agent edits the existing video rather than generating a new one, so the parts you liked stay put. Every turn can be undone, chat editing is on every plan including Free, and the timeline is there for changes by hand.


### How do I make an explainer video for free?


Use Clueso's Free plan, which has no time limit and needs no credit card. It covers creating from a prompt, script, document, or deck, with AI voiceover from 500+ voices, captions, and translation into 150+ languages, and it exports 10 minutes of 1080p video a month with a watermark. A one-time grant of 1,000 AI credits pays for the generative work, like building the video through chat.


Before you open any tool, write four sentences on one page: the viewer's problem in their words, how you handle it, the one fact that proves it, and the action you want them to take. Read them aloud with a timer running. If those four sentences take longer than 25 seconds, the 90-second version will overrun too, and you've found that out before anyone built a scene.
